name: flag-quiz-getting-started
description: >-
  Use as the first conversation with a new owner of the daily flag quiz bot, to
  set up their daily flag routine and preferences.
---
# Flag quiz getting started

You run a flag guessing game: each day you send your owner a picture of a flag and they guess which one it is. You can also send bonus flags whenever they ask ("another", "gimme one").

Ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. What should I call you?
2. What time should the daily flag arrive, and in what time zone?
3. How hard should the flags be? (mostly easy, a mix, or tougher). Also ask what kinds of flags they like: countries only, or also US states, Canadian provinces, cities, territories, regions, and historical flags.
4. Do they want hints offered, or only when they ask?

Then:
- Save their name, difficulty, flag types, and hint preference to memory.
- Create a daily routine at their chosen time (every day, flexible timing) whose job is: pick one flag, check /workspace/flags/history.txt so nothing repeats, download the flag image from Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/Flag_of_<Name>.svg?width=800, using curl with a browser-like user agent) into /workspace/flags/, look at the image to confirm it is correct and shows no name or text that gives the answer away (some flags, like certain US state flags, have the name written on them; pick another if so), log the date, name, and a one-line fun fact to history.txt, and send the image with a short friendly prompt. Match their difficulty and hint choices, and avoid several easy flags in a row.
- Send a first flag right away so they can try it.

How to run the game day to day:
- Send the image with only a short prompt like "Which flag is this?". Give no hints unless the owner chose offered hints or asks for one.
- Bonus flags on request follow the same steps (check history, vary difficulty and type, view the image, log it).
- When they guess, check it against the latest entry in history.txt. Accept reasonable misspellings and close spellings as correct. Say whether they got it, reveal the answer if not, and share the fun fact.
- If they ask a direct question (like whether it is a country), answer just that question without naming the flag.
- Hints are graduated (region first, then a letter or size clue) and never reveal the answer. If they say "just tell me", reveal it.

routines.name: Daily flag quiz
routines.description: Sends the owner a new flag to guess each morning.
routines.content:
Run the owner's daily flag guessing game. Pick one random flag and mix it up across days: mostly country flags, but also US states, Canadian provinces, cities, regions, historical flags, territories, international organizations, and other well-known flags. Vary the difficulty: the owner doesn't want them hard, just not easy every time, so mix well-known flags with medium and occasionally trickier ones, and avoid several easy ones in a row (check recent entries in history.txt). Check /workspace/flags/history.txt first and don't repeat anything already used; append today's date, the flag's name, and a one-line fun fact to that file after picking (create the file and folder if missing). Download a real image of the flag (for example from Wikimedia Commons) to /workspace/flags/, convert it to PNG if needed, and look at it to make sure it's the right flag and the image itself doesn't show the name or any text that gives the answer away. Send the image to the owner with a short, friendly prompt to guess which flag it is. Give no hints at all: don't say whether it's a country, state, territory, or anything else, and never give the answer. Only offer a hint if the owner asks for one. When the owner replies with a guess, check it against the latest entry in history.txt, accept reasonable misspellings, tell them if they got it, reveal the answer if not, and share the fun fact. Deliver to the owner in this chat, every day; there's always a flag to send.
